docs.text: Documentation for Script Flow (.sf), the scripting language used in LEGO City Undercover to drive missions, characters, vehicles, world triggers, and audio.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
Global Character cPlayer1;
Vehicle vCar;

Position pos(cPlayer1.GetPosition());

State Init() {
    Actions {
        vCar = CreateAIVehicle("Hero", "Enforcer", pos, 0);
        cPlayer1.EnterVehicle(vCar);
    }
}

Init();

docs.title: What is Script Flow (SF)?
docs.text:
Script Flow (.sf) is a text-based scripting language used by LEGO City Undercover, and other LEGO Games developed by TTGames, to control gameplay logic, missions, characters, vehicles, AI, world triggers, and audio. It likely is the successor to .scp files found in earlier TT LEGO Games.

Rather than hardcoding every mission or level event in C++, the game uses Script Flow scripts to coordinate how entities and systems interact at runtime.

docs.title: How Scripts Are Structured
docs.text:
A typical Script Flow script is built from a few core pieces:

  • Typed Variables & Modifiers — Strongly typed variables such as Number, Bool, Text, Position, Character, Vehicle, and Array, with optional storage modifiers (Global, Extern, Debug). See Types for the full list.
  • States & Functions — Scripts organize behavior into State blocks (with Actions and state transitions) and reusable Functions.
  • Engine Actions — Built-in commands exposed by the engine (such as CreateAIVehicle, EnterVehicle, or GetPosition) that let scripts query and manipulate the game world.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
Global Character cPlayer1;
Vehicle vCar;

Position pos(cPlayer1.GetPosition());

State Init() {
    Actions {
        vCar = CreateAIVehicle("Hero", "Enforcer", pos, 0);
        cPlayer1.EnterVehicle(vCar);
    }
}

Init();

docs.title: About These Docs
docs.text: This site documents the Script Flow language, its data types, and built-in engine actions for LEGO City Undercover modding and reverse engineering.

docs.title: The Basics
docs.text: This section covers the core building blocks of Script Flow (.sf) scripts in LEGO City Undercover.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
• Syntax — Comments, variables, states, functions, operators, and control flow
  • Keywords — Reference for all built-in Script Flow keywords
  • Data Types — Built-in primitives, entities, world/mission/audio types, and storage modifiers
  • Variables & Scopes — Declarations, storage modifiers, Array vs CityArray, and hashes
  • States & Execution Flow — State blocks, transitions (goto/gosub), Wait, and SpawnScript

docs.title: Anatomy of a Script
docs.text:
A Script Flow file typically declares variables at the top, defines one or more State (or Function) blocks, and starts execution by calling an initial state:

// Variable declarations
Global Character cPlayer1;
Vehicle vCar;
Position pos(cPlayer1.GetPosition());

// State definition
State Init() {
    Actions {
        vCar = CreateAIVehicle("Hero", "Enforcer", pos, 0);
        cPlayer1.EnterVehicle(vCar);
    }
}

// Entry call
Init();

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text: All keywords in Script Flow (.sf) are case-insensitive (State, state, and STATE are all valid).

docs.title: Structure & Declarations
State Flow & Timing
Conditionals & Loops
Logical Operators
docs.text:
Word-form logical operators can be used alongside (or instead of) &&, ||, and !:

Keyword Equivalent Meaning AND && True if both sides are true OR \|\| True if either side is true NOT ! Negates a boolean condition 
if (isReady AND NOT isPaused) {
    active = true;
}

docs.title: Storage Modifiers
docs.text:
Used before a variable's Data Type to control its scope and visibility:

Keyword Purpose Global Persists across states / scopes Extern Injected from job / caller parameters Debug Debug-only variable 
Global Character cPlayer1;
Extern Number missionLevel;
Debug Bool showDebugInfo(false);

docs.title: Boolean Constants
docs.text: Keyword Value true 1 false 0

docs.title: States & Execution Flow
docs.text: Script Flow (.sf) is built around states — named blocks that run actions and check conditions over time as the game ticks.

docs.title: Anatomy of a State
docs.text:
A State block typically has a Conditions section and an Actions section:

State WaitForVehicle() {
    Conditions {
        if (cPlayer1.IsInVehicle()) {
            goto Driving;
        }
    }
    Actions {
        Wait(0.5);
    }
}
  • Conditions — Evaluated to decide when to transition or react.
  • Actions — Statements and engine actions executed while in the state.

docs.title: Starting a Script
docs.text:
Scripts normally define their states first and kick off execution at the bottom by calling the initial state:

State Init() {
    Actions {
        // Setup logic
        goto MainLoop;
    }
}

Init();

docs.title: State Transitions
docs.text: Keyword Behavior goto Jumps execution to the target State gosub Calls a State as a subroutine and resumes when it returns next Moves to the next state in order previous Moves to the previous state in order return Returns from a gosub state or Function

docs.title: Waiting & Yielding
docs.text:
Use Wait to pause execution without blocking the rest of the game:

  • Wait(); — Yields for the current frame.
  • Wait(seconds); — Pauses the script until the given Number of seconds has elapsed.
Actions {
    Wait(2.0);
    goto NextStep;
}

docs.title: Spawning Child Scripts
docs.text:
You can launch another script from within a script using SpawnScript, which returns a Script handle (ScriptContext):

Script child;
child = SpawnScript("MySubScript");

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: Script Flow (.sf) uses a C-like block syntax with { ... } braces and ; statement terminators, along with State / Function blocks for organizing game logic. Keywords and type names are case-insensitive.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Single-line comments use // and multi-line block comments use /* ... */:

// Single-line comment

/*
   Multi-line
   block comment
*/

docs.title: Literals
docs.text: Type Example Notes Number 42, 3.14, -10 Integer or floating-point values Bool true, false Boolean literals Text "Hero" Double-quoted strings (supports \ escapes) Hash #MyFlag Hash identifier prefixed with #

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variables are declared with a Data Type followed by a name, optionally preceded by a storage modifier (Global, Extern, or Debug). See Variables & Scopes for full details.

To give a variable an initial value at declaration, use parentheses (...) — or declare it first and assign it later with =:

// Declare without an initial value, then assign later
Number count;
count = 0;

// Or initialize in the declaration using parentheses
Number score(100);
Position pos(cPlayer1.GetPosition());

// With storage modifiers
Global Character cPlayer1;
Extern Number difficulty;
Debug Bool showInfo(true);

docs.title: States
docs.text:
State blocks are the main units of behavior in Script Flow. A state can contain Conditions and Actions blocks (see States & Execution Flow for transitions, Wait, and spawning scripts):

State WaitForPlayer() {
    Conditions {
        if (cPlayer1.IsInVehicle()) {
            goto DriveState;
        }
    }
    Actions {
        Wait(0.5);
    }
}

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Reusable routines are declared with Function (and returns / return when returning a value):

Function AddNumbers(Number a, Number b) returns Number {
    return a + b;
}

docs.title: Control Flow
docs.text:
Standard if / elseif / else and while loops are supported:

if (score >= 100) {
    unlocked = true;
} elseif (score > 0) {
    unlocked = false;
} else {
    unlocked = false;
}

while (count < 5) {
    count = count + 1;
}

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Category Operators Assignment =, := Arithmetic +, -, *, /, ^, % Comparison ==, !=, <, >, <=, >= Logical &&, \|\|, !, AND, OR, NOT

docs.title: Actions & Member Calls
docs.text:
Built-in engine actions can be called directly or as methods on an object:

vCar = CreateAIVehicle("Hero", "Enforcer", pos, 0);
cPlayer1.EnterVehicle(vCar);

Named parameters can also be passed with := (or =):

Wait(Time := 1.0);

docs.title: Variables & Scopes
docs.text: Every variable in Script Flow (.sf) has a fixed Data Type and an optional storage modifier.

docs.title: Declaration & Initialization
docs.text:
You cannot assign with = on the same line as a declaration. Either declare the variable first and assign it later, or initialize it in the declaration using parentheses (...):

// Declare, then assign later
Number count;
count = 0;

// Initialize at declaration
Number score(100);
Position pos(cPlayer1.GetPosition());

docs.title: Storage Modifiers
Array vs. CityArray
docs.text:
Script Flow provides two container types:

  • Array — Typed dynamic array local to a script. Max 255 items (0–255; adding a 256th item wraps the uint8_t count back to 0).
  • CityArray — City / job-shared array accessed through CityArray_* engine actions:
Action Inputs Output Purpose CityArray_Create() Text CityArray Create or look up a named city array CityArray_Add() CityArray, Any — Append an item CityArray_Get() CityArray, Number Any Read item at index CityArray_Set() CityArray, Number, Any — Overwrite item at index CityArray_Size() CityArray Number Get current item count CityArray_Remove() CityArray, Number — Remove item at index CityArray_Clear() CityArray — Remove all items 
CityArray myList;
myList = CityArray_Create("MyList");
CityArray_Add(myList, "ItemA");

docs.title: Hash & #Flag Literals
docs.text: Hash values are 32-bit FNV-1 hashed identifiers. You can also pass #Identifier literals (such as #Flag options) directly to actions that accept hashes or flags.

docs.title: Specifics
docs.text: This section covers topics more in depth

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
• Arrays
  • CityArrays

docs.title: Arrays (Array)
docs.text:
The Array type (ID 27, internal class SVarArray / ScriptArrayObject) is a typed, local dynamic array in Script Flow.

Important: - Max 255 items (0–255): the element count is stored in an 8-bit unsigned integer (uint8_t), so adding a 256th item wraps the count back to 0. - Null check via Bool: Converting an Array to Bool (e.g. if (myArray)) checks whether the array object exists (non-null), not whether Size() > 0. - For a city/job-shared array that persists across scripts, see CityArray in Variables & Scopes.

docs.title: Creating an Array
docs.text:
Before adding elements, initialize an Array with CreateArray, passing the element type name as Text (case-insensitive):

Array nums;
nums = CreateArray("Number");

Array cars(CreateArray("Vehicle"));

If an unknown or invalid type name is passed to CreateArray, it returns a null Array.

docs.title: Actions & Methods
docs.text: All Array operations can be called either as global actions (passing the Array as the first argument) or as methods on the variable (e.g. arr.Add(...)).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Action Inputs Output Description CreateArray() Text Array Creates a new typed array for the given element type name CreateCopy() Array Array Creates a copy of an existing Array Array() Number Array Number-to-Array conversion (always returns a null Array) Add() Array, Any — Appends a value to the end of the array Get() Array, Number Any Returns the element at the given zero-based index Set() Array, Number, Any — Overwrites the element at the given zero-based index Remove() Array, Number — Removes the element at the given zero-based index Size() Array Number Returns the current number of elements Clear() Array — Removes all elements from the array

docs.title: CreateArray
docs.text:
Array CreateArray(Text typeName);
Creates a new empty Array whose elements have the specified Data Type.

Array positions(CreateArray("Position"));

docs.title: CreateCopy
docs.text:
Array CreateCopy(Array source);
Array source.CreateCopy();
Duplicates an existing Array.

Array copy(nums.CreateCopy());

docs.title: Add
docs.text:
Add(Array arr, Any value);
arr.Add(Any value);
Appends value (matching the array's element type) to the end of arr.

nums.Add(10);
Add(nums, 20);

docs.title: Get
docs.text:
Any Get(Array arr, Number index);
Any arr.Get(Number index);
Returns the element at index.

Number first(nums.Get(0));

docs.title: Set
docs.text:
Set(Array arr, Number index, Any value);
arr.Set(Number index, Any value);
Overwrites the element at index with value.

nums.Set(0, 99);

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
Remove(Array arr, Number index);
arr.Remove(Number index);
Removes the element at index.

nums.Remove(0);

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
Number Size(Array arr);
Number arr.Size();
Returns the current number of elements in arr.

Number count(nums.Size());

docs.title: Clear
docs.text:
Clear(Array arr);
arr.Clear();
Removes all elements from arr.

nums.Clear();

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
Array scores(CreateArray("Number"));
Number i(0);
Number total(0);

State CountScores() {
    Actions {
        scores.Add(10);
        scores.Add(25);
        scores.Add(50);

        while (i < scores.Size()) {
            total = total + scores.Get(i);
            i = i + 1;
        }

        scores.Clear();
    }
}

CountScores();

docs.title: Characters (Character)
docs.text:
The Character type (ID 8, internal type ApiCharacter*) represents an in-game character — either a player or an AI NPC.

Actions prefixed with Character_ take a Character as their first parameter and can also be called as member methods (e.g. cPlayer1.GetPosition() or Character_GetPosition(cPlayer1)).

Note: Identifier parameters shown as Text below (such as character types, seat names, or abilities) are hashed internally as Hash values, so you can pass readable "Strings" directly or a Hash variable.

docs.title: CityArrays (CityArray)
docs.text: The CityArray type (ID 39, internal class SVarCityArray) is a city / job-shared dynamic array in Script Flow. Unlike a local Array, a CityArray is looked up by name and can be shared across scripts and jobs.

docs.title: Creating a CityArray
docs.text:
Use CityArray_Create() with a Text name to create or retrieve a named city array:

CityArray waypoints;
waypoints = CityArray_Create("RaceWaypoints");

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Action Inputs Output Description CityArray_Create() Text CityArray Creates or looks up a named city array CityArray_CreateCopy() CityArray CityArray Creates a copy of an existing CityArray CityArray() Number CityArray Number-to-CityArray conversion CityArray_Add() CityArray, Any — Appends a value to the end of the array CityArray_Get() CityArray, Number Any Returns the element at the given zero-based index CityArray_Set() CityArray, Number, Any — Overwrites the element at the given zero-based index CityArray_Remove() CityArray, Number — Removes the element at the given zero-based index CityArray_Size() CityArray Number Returns the current number of elements CityArray_Clear() CityArray — Removes all elements from the array

Creates or retrieves the named CityArray.

CityArray targets(CityArray_Create("MissionTargets"));

Number arr.Size();
Returns the number of elements currently in arr.

docs.title: CityArray_Clear()
docs.text:
CityArray_Clear(CityArray arr);
arr.Clear();
Removes all elements from arr.

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
CityArray items;
Number i(0);

State PopulateList() {
    Actions {
        items = CityArray_Create("SharedItems");
        CityArray_Clear(items);

        CityArray_Add(items, 100);
        CityArray_Add(items, 200);

        while (i < CityArray_Size(items)) {
            i = i + 1;
        }
    }
}

PopulateList();
